memos.headline: MSFT leads with parabolic relative strength; CAT in technical breakdown; JPM quietly strongest risk-adjusted setup
memos.body: I see a clear bifurcation in this universe today. MSFT is the standout leader with +18.2% relative strength vs SPY over 12 weeks and a 26-week return of +33.6%, though its RSI at 73.1 and +19.2% extension above the 50-day mean warn of near-term mean-reversion risk—I'd wait for a pullback toward the 50-day before adding. JPM is my highest-conviction long: only -2.1% off its 52-week high, RSI a comfortable 55.2, low ATR of 1.46%, and massive 12-week relative strength of +16.9% vs SPY. On the avoid side, CAT is in a clear downtrend—RSI 38.4, -10.5% below its 50-day mean, -24.9% drawdown from highs, and -15.6% relative strength over 12 weeks—and I see no reason to step in front of that until it reclaims the 50-day average near ~$895. PG and GOOGL are also showing persistent relative weakness and trading below or near their 50-day means, keeping me sidelined on both.

views.note: Dominant relative strength (+18.2% vs SPY 12w) and strong trend, but RSI 73 and +19% above 50d mean argue for buying a pullback toward ~$430; a close below $430 would change my view.
Best risk-adjusted setup in the universe: only -2.1% from 52w high, RSI 55, low vol (ATR 1.46%), and +16.9% 12w relative strength; invalidated below $345.
Healthy uptrend with +13.1% above 200d mean, RSI 57, and modest +1.0% 12w relative strength; would turn neutral on a close below $310 (roughly the 50d mean).
Mid-range RSI 52 and flat 12w relative strength (-0.7% vs SPY) despite a decent 4w bounce; needs to clear the 52w high area near $236 to get constructive.
26w return of +29.8% is strong but 4w relative strength of -4.9% shows recent loss of leadership; watching whether the 50d mean holds as support.
Trading below its 50d mean, -13.9% drawdown, and -5.5% 12w relative strength vs SPY—clear underperformer; would reconsider above $360.
Worst chart in the universe: RSI 38, -10.5% below 50d mean, -24.9% drawdown, and -15.6% 12w relative strength; no bid until it reclaims ~$895.

RSI 42 and -4.8% below 50d mean suggest a pullback within a longer uptrend (26w +39.2%); could become a buy near $380 support but too early now.
Flat 12w relative strength and RSI 48 leave it directionless; the -5.1% weekly drop is concerning but still above the 200d mean—watching $150 as key support.

memos.headline: NVDA and GOOGL Post Extraordinary Earnings Growth; XOM and PG Show Cash-Flow Compression
memos.body: I am struck by the sheer breadth of earnings acceleration across the mega-cap tech complex this quarter. NVDA's 2027Q2 revenue of $96.22B (+105.9% YoY) at a 62.0% net margin is unlike anything I have seen in hardware at scale, while GOOGL printed a 93.7% net margin on $119.80B of revenue—a nearly 4x YoY net income jump that likely reflects a large one-time gain but still signals formidable operating leverage. AMZN's net income surged 244.9% YoY to $62.65B on a 31.2% net margin, a dramatic expansion from its historically thin-margin profile, and MSFT closed its fiscal year with $35.77B in quarterly net income (+31.3% YoY) at a 39.7% margin. On the other side, XOM's net income fell 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a razor-thin 4.9% margin, and PG's net income declined 15.8% YoY with revenue growing only 1.5%, signaling durable earnings power is under pressure in both names. I would need to see XOM's Q2 filing and PG's organic volume trends before turning constructive on either.

views.note: Revenue doubling YoY to $96.22B with a 62.0% net margin and manageable $33.37B debt is extraordinary earnings power; a margin decline below 50% would change my view.

Net income of $112.19B implies a possible one-time item inflating the 93.7% margin, but even adjusting down, +24.2% revenue growth on minimal $14.79B debt is compelling; I need to verify the composition of that income.
Full-year Q4 revenue of $90.01B (+17.7% YoY) with a 39.7% net margin and only $40.29B debt demonstrates durable, high-quality earnings growth across cloud and AI segments.
Net income of $62.65B (+244.9% YoY) on $200.61B revenue shows massive margin expansion to 31.2%, though $133B in total debt and the sustainability of this margin level warrant monitoring.
Revenue of $109.42B (+16.4% YoY) with a 27.2% net margin is solid, though $82.30B in debt is elevated; I'd want to see Services mix continuing to expand.
Revenue up 24.0% YoY to $20.54B with net income surging 64.9% and a 17.5% margin is impressive cyclical performance, but I am wary of cycle peak risk.
Net income of $21.16B (+41.2% YoY) at a 36.9% margin is strong, but $460.52B in total debt and credit-cycle sensitivity keep me from going outright long.
Revenue essentially flat at $112.03B (+0.4% YoY) with only a 4.9% net margin despite a 61% net income rebound suggests the earnings base remains fragile.
Net income collapsed 45.8% YoY to $4.18B on a 4.9% margin with stagnant 2.4% revenue growth—classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for until commodity prices stabilize.
Revenue grew just 1.5% YoY to $21.20B while net income fell 15.8%, compressing the margin to 14.4%; I need to see volume-driven top-line acceleration before reconsidering.

memos.headline: Fed Paused at 3.75% but Sticky 3.3% CPI and Rising Long Yields Signal a Hawkish Hold — Favor Defensives and Banks Over Duration-Sensitive Growth
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in pause mode: the upper bound has been flat at 3.75% for three months after 75 bps of cuts over the prior year, and the labor market is tightening with unemployment at 4.10%, down 20 bps over both three- and twelve-month horizons. The problem is inflation — headline CPI is running at 3.3% YoY, well above target, and the long end is repricing accordingly with the 10y yield at 4.73%, up 51 bps over the past year and 28 bps in just three months. The 10y-2y spread at +47 bps is positive but narrowing, consistent with a late-cycle environment where the market doubts further easing. This regime — paused Fed, sticky inflation, rising term premium — is unfriendly to long-duration growth equities and supportive of banks earning on a positively-sloped curve and defensive staples. A CPI print dropping below 3.0% or unemployment rising above 4.3% would shift my call toward renewed easing and a more constructive duration stance.

views.note: Positive yield curve (47 bps), paused Fed, and strong labor market support net interest income for large banks.
Defensive staples benefit from a late-cycle pause regime with rising long yields pressuring growth multiples.
Sticky inflation and solid employment support nominal demand, but rising real yields and no clear cyclical acceleration limit upside.
Labor market is firm but the hawkish hold and rising long-end rates could weigh on capex-sensitive cyclicals if the pause extends.
10y yield up 51 bps YoY to 4.73% with no easing in sight compresses long-duration growth multiples most aggressively.
Quality duration name faces headwinds from rising long yields but strong cash flows provide a buffer versus pure-growth peers.
Similar to AAPL — high-quality but duration-sensitive; the macro regime argues for patience rather than adding here.
Consumer-facing growth name with high duration sensitivity; 3.3% CPI and 4.73% 10y yield are a tough combination for multiples.
Ad cyclicality is a modest positive given low unemployment, but rising discount rates keep me from getting constructive.
Defensive healthcare with pricing power in an inflationary pause regime; less rate-sensitive than tech growth.

memos.headline: Post-Earnings Sentiment Split: MSFT/AMZN/NVDA Momentum vs. AAPL/GOOGL Drag
memos.body: I am reading a clear bifurcation in post-earnings price reactions across the mega-cap universe this cycle. MSFT (+15.5%), AMZN (+15.3%), and NVDA (+8.7%) all printed strong positive reactions on their results filings, suggesting narrative momentum that may still have legs, while AAPL (-7.4%) and GOOGL (-7.1%) saw sharp negative reactions that signal deteriorating sentiment. CAT (+5.6%) and JPM (+2.5%) posted modest positive reactions, indicating constructive but not euphoric tone. PG (-1.9%) and UNH (+1.2%) were muted, consistent with defensive names where sentiment is largely priced. My concern is that the crowded positive tone around MSFT and AMZN after double-digit pops may already be fully reflected, so I have higher conviction on NVDA where the earnings beat is only two days old and the narrative is freshest.

views.note: Freshest positive catalyst with +8.7% earnings reaction just yesterday plus a material agreement filing on 8/17 suggesting expanding financial commitments.
Massive +15.5% earnings reaction signals strong fundamental narrative, but nearly a month has passed so positive sentiment is likely well-absorbed by now.
The +15.3% post-earnings pop was emphatic, but like MSFT the move is almost a month old and crowded positive tone is a caution flag.
A -7.4% earnings-day drop is a clear negative sentiment shift; with no subsequent positive catalyst filed, the narrative remains impaired.
The -7.1% earnings reaction and a subsequent 8-K on 8/10 with no visible positive price catalyst suggest sentiment has not recovered.
Solid +5.6% earnings reaction and Reg FD disclosure suggest constructive industrial sentiment, though the move is modest and aging.
Mild +2.5% earnings reaction and routine corporate filings suggest stable but unexciting sentiment; no clear directional edge.
A -1.9% earnings reaction plus management changes create mixed signals; defensive tone is neither improving nor deteriorating meaningfully.
Tepid +1.2% earnings reaction over a month ago leaves little sentiment signal to act on today.
No 8-K filings in the evidence set; I have no sentiment signal to form a view and remain on the sideline.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Plunges Nearly 50% in Three Months—Geopolitical Tail Risks Receding but NVDA Export-Control Overhang Persists
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index has collapsed to 166.87, down roughly 49% over both one- and three-month horizons, while the VIX has fallen to 14.51 (−22% m/m) and HY OAS has tightened to 2.63% (−18 bps m/m). This combination signals that the market is pricing out near-term policy shocks—sanctions escalation, tariff surprises, or energy-supply disruptions—at a pace I find somewhat aggressive given that WTI at $84.81 remains elevated and NVDA filed a Reg FD 8-K on Aug 17 that may relate to ongoing China AI-chip export-control compliance. I have moderate conviction that the de-escalation in policy uncertainty is a structural shift benefiting domestically oriented names (JPM, PG) and global capex plays (CAT), but I remain cautious on NVDA where a single tightening of export rules could materially reset the revenue outlook. A re-imposition or broadening of semiconductor export controls toward China would be the key policy action that changes my view across the tech complex.

views.note: Aug 17 Reg FD filing and persistent export-control overhang on China AI-chip sales keep me from getting constructive despite falling macro uncertainty.
Steep drop in policy uncertainty and a steepening yield curve (+13 bps m/m on 10y-2y) support NII expansion; two recent 8-Ks suggest active investor communication.
Falling policy uncertainty and stable oil prices favor global infrastructure capex, though I lack detail on the Aug 4 Reg FD disclosure to have higher conviction.
Three Reg FD filings in July suggest proactive guidance; collapsing policy uncertainty and tight credit spreads reduce input-cost and FX volatility risk for a global consumer staple.
WTI at $84.81 is supportive but down 8% over three months; energy-security tailwinds appear to be fading alongside broader geopolitical de-escalation.
No company-specific filings in the evidence set; China supply-chain concentration remains a latent risk even as headline policy uncertainty drops.
